text:
ops-bot: [PAGER] streaming-api: high tail latency detected (p95 480ms -> 1.8s, p99 1.2s -> 6.4s). SLO: 95% < 300ms. Auto page to #incidents oncall.

alice (oncall): saw the pager. Investigating now. Any known deploys?

charlie (sre): No deploys in the last 30m per deploy-bot. Graphs show a sharp increase at 22:10 UTC. Connections to streaming-proxy-01 show TCP write stalls.

priya (infra): I'm seeing elevated socket write queues on the proxy nodes, kernel tcp_sndbuf at capacity. Possible slow consumer/backpressure from downstream. Kernel logs: `NETDEV_TX_BUSY` spikes.

devin (eng-runtime): Client-side acks look normal. The larger traces show chunking delays: the runtime is emitting chunks but proxy write syscall is blocking for >200ms intermittently. This matches SSE/WebSocket slow-write behavior.

sam (support): Customer impact: 3 enterprise customers (acct-92, acct-231) reported hung streams and UI spinner. We should notify them ASAP with ETA.

alice (oncall): Triage plan: 1) identify which proxy pool / AZ is impacted; 2) try to drain and failover traffic; 3) enable fast-fallback (non-streaming) route for affected customers; 4) scale proxies / increase write buffers.

charlie (sre): Correlation: spikes originate from eu-west region proxies. `proxy-autoscaler` hasn't scaled because CPU is low; this is IO bound. Investigating network saturations on egress NICs.

priya (infra): K8s node metrics show `tx_packets` backlog and `ifconfig` shows dropped packets rising. Potential noisy neighbor? I'll look for noisy pods.

devin (eng-runtime): Workaround suggestion: flip routing for streaming traffic to a sibling region's proxy pool (eu-central) with lower connection queue. Or enable immediate `streaming-fallback: true` which serves non-streaming (batched) responses.

alice (oncall): Do we have a runbook step for proxy slow-write?

charlie (sre): Runbook: `incidents/runbooks/streaming-slowwrite.md` (follow steps: scale proxy replicas, toggle connection_linger off, increase proxy_write_buffer to 256k, reroute). I'm running the quick checks now.

ops-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-4859992222. Paging oncall: alice.

priya (infra): Found a suspect: `log-collector` sidecar pod in eu-west-3 is sending bursts, saturating egress on node-7. I am cordoning node-7 and will evict pods gracefully. Command: `kubectl cordon node-7 && kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`

alice (oncall): Proceed with drain. Notify customers about temporary reconnects.

sam (support): Drafting customer message: "We're seeing streaming disruption in EU. Engineers are actively mitigating. You may see re-connects; normal service should resume within ~15-30m." Want sign-off.

devin (eng-runtime): While node drain runs, enabling fallback route for affected tenants. Command: `redwoodctl routes set --tenant acct-92,acct-231 --route streaming,fallback=true`

alice (oncall): Execed the route flip. Confirming metrics.

charlie (sre): After drain started, proxy write stalls reduced markedly on node-7. p95 back to ~320ms, p99 ~1.1s but trending down. Good signal.

priya (infra): Eviction finished, node-7 replaced noisy pod. Egress drops normalized. I increased proxy write buffer on eu-west proxies: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem='4096 87380 262144'` and reloaded proxies.

ops-bot: Automated alert suppressed (metric back to normal) but incident remains open for postmortem.

alice (oncall): Customer update drafted and sent by sam. Customers confirmed streams reconnecting. Any lingering issues?

devin (eng-runtime): We saw a single proxy instance flip its circuit breaker due to repeated EAGAIN on write; I disabled aggressive circuit for streams temporarily: set `proxy.write_retry_backoff=100ms -> 50ms` to reduce timeouts while buffer replenishes.

charlie (sre): Adding temporary mitigation: increase number of proxy workers by 30% in eu-west (scaling group `proxy-eu-west` +30%).

priya (infra): Autoscaling policy update queued: change scale policy from CPU-based to include egress-saturation/k8s queue metrics. Need to follow up in infra backlog.

alice (oncall): Current status: mitigations applied (drain, route-flip, buffer bump, cb tweak, scale). p95=280-350ms, p99=700-1100ms. Customer impact reduced to intermittent reconnects.

sam (support): Customers acked and gave thumbs up. No new tickets for 20m.

devin (eng-runtime): Logging note: captured a stack of blocked write syscalls on the proxy process. Will attach traces to incident. Example snippet:

```
proxy write() blocked for 312ms -> write returned EAGAIN after 4 retries
goroutine 78 [IO wait]:
  net.(*netFD).write(...)
  net.(*conn).Write(0xc0003aa000, 0xc0002ab000, 0x1f2)
```

charlie (sre): Root cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor causing egress saturation on node causing proxy write buffers to fill -> socket backpressure -> app-level stalls -> p99 spike. Secondary factor: circuit breaker too aggressive for streaming semantics.

alice (oncall): Actions for postmortem: 1) formal RCA with timeline; 2) relax circuit breaker defaults for streaming; 3) add egress as autoscaling signal; 4) improve runbook with `streaming-fallback` pre-steps; 5) customer communication template.

priya (infra): I'll open infra ticket to push sysctl defaults and update autoscaler.

devin (eng-runtime): I'll submit PR to change cb defaults and add metric alerts for socket write latency.

charlie (sre): I'll own the incident writeup and link graphs/traces.

alice (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing to charlie for postmortem and follow-ups. Oncall clear for now.

ops-bot: Incident status: ASSESSMENT -> MITIGATED. Incident owner: charlie.

charlie (sre): acked. Will follow up in postmortem doc and schedule downtime review if needed.

sam (support): Closing loop with customers in 2 hours and will escalate if anything recurs.

ops-bot: Thread auto-archived in 72h for postmortem tracking.
